papers.title: Evidence for Normal Neutrino Ordering with Combined Atmospheric Neutrino Experiments
papers.abstract: We present a combined analysis of the latest publicly available atmospheric neutrino data from Super-Kamiokande including all data-taking stages previous to the gadolinium phase, IceCube-DeepCore, and the six-detection-unit configuration of KM3NeT/ORCA. Our fit uses all event samples simultaneously and treats the systematic uncertainties shared among experiments as fully correlated, while detector-response uncertainties are modeled independently for each experiment. %We measure The combined data constrain the atmospheric oscillation parameters to $\Delta m^2_{31} = 2.44^{+0.06}_{-0.04} \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{eV}^2$ and $\sin^2\theta_{23} = 0.52^{+0.03}_{-0.04}$, with a precision of $2.2\%$ and $6.1\%$, respectively, which is competitive with current accelerator-based measurements, and independently constrain the $CP$-violating phase to $\delta_{CP} = 1.30^{+0.24}_{-0.28}~\pi$. Finally, comparing the orderings of the neutrino mass spectrum, we find a preference for the normal ordering with $\Delta\chi^2 = 11.0$; further calibrated with pseudoexperiments, we exclude the inverted ordering at $99.95\%$ confidence level ($3.3\sigma$).
papers.reason: Presents a combined analysis of atmospheric neutrino data from Super-K, IceCube-DeepCore, and KM3NeT/ORCA, yielding strong evidence for normal mass ordering and precise oscillation parameters.

papers.title: Fano formula for resonance poles in the Jost--random-phase approximation: Breit--Wigner-type peaks, Fano dips, and Fano-type peaks in $^{16}$O and $^{208}$Pb
papers.abstract: Fano's formula is derived for a resonance pole of the strength function in the continuum random-phase approximation formulated within the Jost function framework (Jost-RPA). At a pole, the residue of the transition-amplitude vector of the open channels lies along the Takagi vector of the pole for every external field. Of the background, the amplitude vector without the pole term, only the component along the Takagi vector therefore interferes with the resonance, and the strength function can be written exactly in Fano's form for several continuum channels. In this form $q$ is complex and energy dependent, and the modulus $p$ of the cosine of the angle between the Takagi vector and the background serves as Fano's $|\rho|$. In an idealized form of Fano's model, $q$ and $p$ reduce to Fano's $q$ and to the overlap $|\rho|$ of Fano and Cooper. A second exact form separates a Fano term and a Breit-Wigner term, the part of the resonance that does not interfere with the background. Three patterns follow: Breit-Wigner-type peaks for $p^2\simeq0$, Fano dips, and Fano-type peaks for $p^2\simeq1$. A negative real part of the complex transition probability, the residue of the response function at the pole, is equivalent to Fano's condition $|q|<1$ for a dip at the resonance energy, evaluated at the complex conjugate of the pole energy. Earlier Jost-RPA analyses were made only for $^{16}$O. The analysis is applied to $^{16}$O and to $^{208}$Pb, with up to 62 open channels. It attributes the dips found earlier in $^{16}$O to the interference of single poles with their backgrounds, and it shows in both nuclei Fano dips, Fano-type peaks, and poles whose pattern changes with the field. In $^{208}$Pb, narrow poles near the broad poles of the giant dipole resonances produce Fano-type peaks with dips in the field of each resonance. The patterns are not determined by the collectivity indicators of the poles.
papers.reason: Derives Fano's formula for resonance poles within the Jost-RPA framework and analyzes continuum channels in $^{16}$O and $^{208}$Pb, directly addressing nuclear response and electroweak reaction mechanisms.

papers.title: Form factors and weak decays of $\Lambda_b\to\Lambda_c^*(2595)$ and $\Xi_b\to\Xi_c^*(2790)$
papers.reason: Calculates electroweak transition form factors of $\Lambda_b$ and $\Xi_b$ baryons using QCD sum rules, providing direct inputs for heavy-baryon semileptonic decays relevant to weak interaction physics.

papers.title: Isospin breaking in $\rho\pi\pi$ couplings: $\rho^{+,0}$ width difference and muon $g-2$
papers.abstract: The dominant contribution to the hadronic vaccum polarization (HVP) of the muon $g-2$ can be calculated using the hadronic spectrum in $\tau^- \to \pi^-\pi^0\nu_{\tau}$ decay, provided isospin breaking (IB) corrections are properly accounted for. Among these corrections, IB in the $\rho\pi\pi$ coupling has been pointed out as a missing ingredient. In this work, we calculate this IB effect within the impulse approximation using a symmetry-preserving framework based on Dyson-Schwinger and Bethe-Salpeter equations, incorporating fully dressed quark propagators and meson Bethe-Salpeter amplitudes. We then estimate its effect in the HVP contribution to the muon $g-2$. As a natural extension, we also compute the IB in the ratio of $\phi K^+K^-/\phi K^0\bar{K^0}$ couplings and compare with existing data. We obtain a coupling ratio $g_{\rho^0\pi^+\pi^-}/g_{\rho^+\pi^+\pi^0} = 1.0024(17)(1)$, which yields an isospin-breaking correction of $\Delta a_\mu^{\mathrm{HVP,LO}}[\rho\pi\pi] = -2.32(1.64)\times 10^{-10}$ to the two-pion contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment extracted from $\tau$ decay data.
papers.reason: Calculates isospin-breaking corrections in the $\rho\pi\pi$ coupling using Dyson-Schwinger and Bethe-Salpeter equations and evaluates their impact on the muon $g-2$ HVP contribution from $\tau$ decays.

papers.title: Combining Pumping and Absorption Effects in Neutrino Oscillation Probabilities: A Non-Hermitian Framework
papers.abstract: We study two-flavour neutrino oscillations in which a coherent off-diagonal interaction from a complex background field coexists with an absorptive channel acting on a single mass eigenstate. Since the two do not commute, the effective Hamiltonian is non-normal and oscillations and damping no longer factorise. We formulate the dynamics both as the no-jump sector of a Lindblad evolution and through biorthogonal diagonalisation, and obtain the evolution operator of our model in closed form. The model interpolates between quasi-global damping, standard invisible decay, and a critical point with polynomial-times-exponential evolution; for initially pure states it describes norm loss rather than decoherence. Comparing neutrinos and antineutrinos in the same background, with the mixing phase $\phi$ reversed and the background phase $\delta$ fixed, we derive closed-form $CP$, $CPT$ and $T$ asymmetries. The $CPT$ asymmetries arise only from this phase assignment. In contrast, the $T$ asymmetry, which is forbidden in unitary two-flavour oscillations, is independent of the prescription: it arises only through the non-normal structure, is proportional to the absorptive coupling, and vanishes only when $\delta+\phi=n\pi$. For equal initial populations the net neutrino--antineutrino asymmetry vanishes identically, while a non-zero flavour asymmetry survives and requires a non-normal Hamiltonian.
papers.reason: Formulates a non-Hermitian framework combining absorption and coherent backgrounds to study neutrino oscillation probabilities, CP/CPT/T asymmetries, and norm loss.

papers.title: Correlations in oscillation data and their impact on neutrino mixing models
papers.abstract: With increasing precision of neutrino experiments, complete correlation among the oscillation parameters will scrutinize theoretical neutrino mass and mixing models. Using available 1D--3D global-fit datasets, we construct a multidimensional $\tilde{\chi}^2$ function that provides a conservative estimate of the full six-dimensional parameter correlations. In our approach, we delineate the model-constrained parameter space by combining the interpolated experimental data with the analytical relations implied by a given mixing scheme. We identify $\tilde{\chi}^2_{\text{min}}$, corresponding to the optimal agreement attainable for parameter points satisfying the model. Applying this framework to several schemes ($\text{TM}_{1,2}$, $\mu1,2$--$\tau1,2$) yields generally better fits for IO than for NO, with the $\mu1$--$\tau1$ scheme under IO providing the best overall fit. While $\mu1,2$--$\tau1,2$ and $\text{TM}_1$ schemes perform significantly better than $\text{TM}_2$, the latter is excluded at $>3\sigma$ C.L. using NuFIT~v6.1 data. We further evaluate the implications of these correlation-respecting constraints on the effective neutrino mass observables relevant to tritium $\beta$-decay ($m_{\beta}$) and neutrinoless double $\beta$-decay ($m_{\beta\beta}$). The proposed approach can be readily extended to test any theoretical framework that predicts algebraic relations among neutrino oscillation parameters, and we provide a GitHub starter kit.
papers.reason: Examines experimental oscillation parameter correlations and their impact on theoretical mass/mixing models (TM, mu-tau symmetry) and beta/double-beta decay observables.

summary.tldr: A multidimensional $\tilde{\chi}^2$ method reconstructs 6D oscillation parameter correlations from NuFIT data, tightly constraining neutrino mixing models and excluding trimaximal $\mathrm{TM}_2$ mixing at $>3\sigma$ once JUNO is included.
summary.novel_idea: Rather than testing discrete flavor-symmetry mixing sum rules against decoupled 1D or 2D parameter intervals, the authors construct an interpolated continuous multi-dimensional likelihood surface from public 1D--3D NuFIT datasets to estimate the full 6D parameter correlations. This permits projection of model-specific algebraic constraints directly onto the correlated experimental manifold to identify genuine optimal fit points ($\tilde{\chi}^2_{\text{min}}$).
summary.method: The framework interpolates available 1D, 2D, and 3D $\Delta\chi^2$ data from NuFIT v6.0 and v6.1 (including initial 59-day JUNO measurements of $\theta_{12}$ and $\Delta m^2_{21}$). Analytical sum rules for $\mathrm{TM}_1$, $\mathrm{TM}_2$, and $\mu-\tau$ reflection symmetries ($\mu 1-\tau 1$, $\mu 2-\tau 2$) are implemented as hypersurface constraints during numerical minimization over the correlated parameter space. The resulting constraints are propagated to predictions for $m_{\beta}$ and $m_{\beta\beta}$.
key_results: Inverted ordering (IO) generally yields better fits than normal ordering (NO) for the surveyed schemes, with $\mu 1-\tau 1$ under IO giving the best fit overall ($\tilde{\chi}^2_{\text{min}} = 0.12$).

The updated solar precision from JUNO in NuFIT v6.1 decisively rules out $\mathrm{TM}_2$ mixing at $>3\sigma$ C.L. ($\tilde{\chi}^2 > 9$) for both mass orderings due to the $\theta_{12}-\theta_{13}$ constraint.
$\mathrm{TM}_1$ remains fully viable under NuFIT v6.1 with $\tilde{\chi}^2_{\text{min}} \sim 0.63$ (NO) and $0.78$ (IO).
Correlations significantly contract the allowed $m_{\beta\beta}$ bands at low lightest-neutrino mass $m_0$ in NO, though the impact in IO is comparatively mild.
summary.why_it_matters: While primarily focused on discrete flavor symmetry model-building (a tangential topic for cross-section modelers), the public Mathematica tool provides a valuable, ready-to-use pipeline for testing any BSM or oscillation hypothesis that introduces algebraic relations among PMNS parameters against correlated global data.
summary.caveats: The 6D correlation surface is an approximation reconstructed from lower-dimensional projections because full 6D likelihood chains from global-fit collaborations are not publicly available; cosmological bounds on $\sum m_\nu$ are not incorporated.

papers.title: Hadronization in QCD and Fragmentation Functions
papers.abstract: The hadronization of quarks and gluons is reviewed within the framework of collinear parton-to-hadron fragmentation functions closely associated with the notion of factorization in hard scattering processes in QCD. The state-of-the-art in calculating both the scale evolution of fragmentation functions and the partonic cross sections pertinent to their determination from data up to next-to-next-to-leading order accuracy is presented. Potential improvements up to next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic order are outlined as well. All relevant experimental data sets for single-inclusive pion, kaon, and unidentified charged hadron production are listed. The most recent sets of fragmentation functions and their uncertainties extracted from these data in global QCD analyses utilizing various different strategies are presented and compared to each other.
papers.reason: Reviews collinear parton-to-hadron fragmentation functions and global QCD analyses of hadronization, providing crucial context for cross-section modeling and factorization.

summary.tldr: A comprehensive review of collinear parton-to-hadron fragmentation functions, their NNLO evolution and coefficient functions, sum rules, and current global extractions for pions, kaons, and charged hadrons.
summary.novel_idea: This state-of-the-art review consolidates recent theoretical advancements up to NNLO in time-like DGLAP evolution and hard-scattering cross sections, highlighting the resolution of previous ambiguities in the time-like splitting functions via SCET and all-order reciprocity relations, while synthesizing tension patterns among modern global fits (MAPFF, BDSSV, NPC, JAM).
summary.method: The authors review pQCD collinear factorization applied to single-inclusive $e^+e^-$ annihilation (SIA), semi-inclusive DIS (SIDIS), and hadron production in $pp$ collisions. They detail both $z$-space (Runge-Kutta) and Mellin-moment solution schemes of matrix RGEs, matching conditions for heavy flavors in variable flavor number schemes (VFNS), and systematic data selections across collider experiments.
key_results: Singlet fragmentation distributions ($D_\Sigma$) are tightly pinned down across all modern fits by LEP/SLD data at $\mu = M_Z$, but severe discrepancies persist in gluon fragmentation ($D_g$).

Unfavored fragmentation functions, particularly $D_{\bar{u}}^{\pi^+}$ and $D_{s+\bar{s}}^{\pi^+}$, show poor agreement across fits at low $z$ ($z \lesssim 0.2$), heavily influenced by differing flavor/isospin-symmetry assumptions in parameterizations.

Discrepancies in the gluon FF are traced to persistent tensions between RHIC and LHC $pp \to h X$ measurements, which await resolution via global fits utilizing newly available NNLO $pp$ calculations.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to high-energy neutrino-nucleus scattering: understanding hadronization and fragmentation functions is essential for transitioning from shallow to deep-inelastic scattering (SIS/DIS) and benchmarking hadron formation and intranuclear cascade models inside neutrino event generators such as GENIE, GiBUU, and NuWro.
summary.caveats: Focuses strictly on collinear, integrated fragmentation of light hadrons; TMD fragmentation, di-hadron FFs, and heavy-flavor hadronization (e.g., $D$-meson formation) are outside the scope.

We perform a detector-level analysis with an integrated luminosity of $1~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, assuming unpolarized muon beams, and derive median expected $95\%$ confidence-level upper limits on the visible signal cross section ranging from approximately $0.027$ to $0.113~\mathrm{fb}$, corresponding to limits on the mixing strength parameter $|U_{\mu N}|^2$ ranging from $6.7	imes10^{-6}$ to $8.3	imes10^{-5}$ for six benchmark points. summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts the BSM neutrino program at future high-energy lepton colliders, providing concrete benchmark sensitivity for intermediate-mass Dirac HNLs and highlighting the pitfall of assuming event yields translate directly into exclusion power when combining distinct production topologies.
summary.caveats: Analysis neglects beam-induced backgrounds (BIB) characteristic of muon colliders, assumes unpolarized beams, uses a generic detector card rather than a full Muon Collider Detector simulation, and restricts HNL decays to the prompt regime.

papers.title: Reconciling anomalous quadrupole deformation in $^{200,202}$Hg with Coulomb excitation
papers.abstract: Stable isotopes of mercury, with two fewer protons than magic lead, are found experimentally to exhibit oblate deformation, similar to neighbouring platinum isotopes. These isotopes are of special interest due to the use of $^{199}$Hg as an experimental laboratory for electric dipole moment searches, which are a powerful test of charge-parity ($CP$) violation and the interpretation of which depends critically on the quadrupole and octopule shapes of the underlying nucleus. It is observed that the ratio between experimental quadrupole moments and electric quadrupole transition strengths exceed physical limits, placing uncertainty on this underlying shape. In an effort to resolve this situation, a Coulomb excitation experiment was performed to remeasure the spectroscopic quadrupole moment ($Q_s(2^+_1)$) of $^{200}$Hg and $^{202}$Hg utilising $^{48}$Ti and $^{120}$Sn targets. The values obtained were $Q_s(2^+_1)$ $^{200,202}$Hg = $0.52(14)$, $0.63(10)$ eb, lying within physical limits defined by $B(E2)$ values but still consistent with near axially-symmetric oblate deformation. A systematic study of nuclei indicates that, as with neighbouring Pt isotopes, $^{200,202}$Hg are strongly oblate deformed, albeit without fully developing into an axial rotor.
papers.reason: Performs a Coulomb excitation experiment to remeasure spectroscopic quadrupole moments of $^{200,202}$Hg, resolving deformation anomalies relevant to nuclear structure and atomic EDM interpretations.

summary.tldr: Coulomb excitation remeasurements of $^{200,202}\mathrm{Hg}$ resolve previous unphysical spectroscopic quadrupole moments, establishing moderate oblate collectivity within physical rigid-rotor limits.
summary.novel_idea: Prior literature reported $Q_s(2^+_1)$ values for $^{200,202}\mathrm{Hg}$ that severely exceeded the maximum physical limits established by $B(E2)$ transition strengths for an axial rotor. By employing inverse kinematics with heavy Hg beams on $^{48}\mathrm{Ti}$ and $^{120}\mathrm{Sn}$ targets at ATLAS, this experiment removes target-excitation ambiguities and brings the quadrupole moments back into consistency with collective systematics.
summary.method: Beams of $^{200,202}\mathrm{Hg}$ at $\sim 3.9~\mathrm{MeV/u}$ were Coulomb-excited on $^{48}\mathrm{Ti}$ and $^{120}\mathrm{Sn}$ targets. Reaction products were tagged with an annular double-sided silicon strip detector (DSSD) in coincidence with de-excitation $\gamma$-rays measured in Gammasphere (74 HPGe detectors). Matrix elements and $Q_s(2^+_1)$ were deduced via coupled-channels minimization in GOSIA/GOSIAFitter.
key_results: Obtained spectroscopic quadrupole moments $Q_s(2^+_1) = 0.52(14)~e\mathrm{b}$ for $^{200}\mathrm{Hg}$ and $0.63(10)~e\mathrm{b}$ for $^{202}\mathrm{Hg}$ (literature-constrained fit).
Confirmed oblate deformation ($Q_s > 0$) while strictly satisfying the physical limit $|Q_s(2^+_1)| \le Q_{\mathrm{rot}}(2^+_1)$ derived from $B(E2)$ values.
Potential energy surface calculations confirm shallow oblate minima with near-zero octupole deformation ($\beta_3 \approx 0$), implying a suppressed atomic Schiff moment.
summary.why_it_matters: Crucial for atomic EDM searches in $^{199}\mathrm{Hg}$ (which constrain $T$- and $CP$-violating BSM physics via the nuclear Schiff moment), as the extracted Schiff moment depends directly on core quadrupole and octupole deformations.
summary.caveats: Does not measure the odd-mass isotope $^{199}\mathrm{Hg}$ directly; deformation properties must be inferred across isotopes. Also, $B(E3)$ strengths could not be extracted directly from this dataset.

Five benchmarks spanning $m_a=100$--$1000\GeV$ are generated at $g_{a\gamma\gamma}=0.01\TeV^{-1}$ and flavor-universal pseudoscalar neutrino couplings $y_

Assuming a 1\% background normalization uncertainty, a cut-based photon-line selection gives projected 95\% sensitivity to $g_{a\gamma\gamma}\simeq0.039$--$0.045\TeV^{-1}$ at $3\TeV$ and $0.0137$--$0.0140\TeV^{-1}$ at $10\TeV$. A ROOT/TMVA gradient-boosted decision tree with validation-fixed thresholds reaches held-out AUC values of $0.9967$--$0.9993$ and $g_{95}=0.0192$--$0.0400\TeV^{-1}$ at $3\TeV$ and $0.0122$--$0.0144\TeV^{-1}$ at $10\TeV$. papers.reason: Studies mono-photon signatures and invisible decays of axion-like particles into neutrinos at muon colliders, highly relevant to BSM searches.

summary.tldr: Projections for mono-photon searches $\mu^+\mu^- \to \gamma a (\to \nu\bar{\nu})$ at 3 and 10 TeV muon colliders constrain $g_{a\gamma\gamma} \gtrsim 0.012~\mathrm{TeV}^{-1}$, supplemented by an HNL diphoton feasibility check.
summary.method: Signal benchmarks ($m_a = 100$--$1000~\mathrm{GeV}$, $g_{a\gamma\gamma} = 0.01~\mathrm{TeV}^{-1}$, $y_\nu = 0.1, 0.3$) were simulated using MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, Pythia 8, and Delphes for $\sqrt{s}=3~\mathrm{TeV}$ ($1~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$) and $10~\mathrm{TeV}$ ($10~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$). Background discrimination was tested with cut-based photon-line windows and TMVA BDTG classifiers using photon $p_T$, $\eta_\gamma$, and recoil mass. A distinct parton-level exercise explores an HNL-mediated diphoton signature.
key_results: For $\mathrm{BR}(a\to\nu\bar{\nu}) > 99.995\%$, the cut-based analysis yields 95% expected sensitivity of $g_{a\gamma\gamma} \simeq 0.039$--$0.045~\mathrm{TeV}^{-1}$ at $3~\mathrm{TeV}$ and $0.0137$--$0.0140~\mathrm{TeV}^{-1}$ at $10~\mathrm{TeV}$.

The BDTG classifier reaches held-out sensitivities of $g_{95} = 0.0192$--$0.0400~\mathrm{TeV}^{-1}$ ($3~\mathrm{TeV}$) and $0.0122$--$0.0144~\mathrm{TeV}^{-1}$ ($10~\mathrm{TeV}$), with AUC values exceeding 0.996.
Sensitivities are reported strictly as expected reach rather than formal exclusions because the extreme BDTG signal tails contain only 2--41 unweighted background events.
summary.why_it_matters: Relevant for BSM phenomenological searches involving neutrinos and ALPs/HNLs at future multi-TeV muon colliders, highlighting the power of mono-photon recoil kinematics.
summary.caveats: Uses a phenomenological low-energy Lagrangian where the unsuppressed $y_\nu$ coupling to chiral neutrinos violates $SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ gauge invariance without an explicit UV sterile completion; simulation omits beam-induced backgrounds and forward detector tags.

papers.title: Femtoscopic correlation functions between the lightest charmed hadrons
papers.abstract: Femtoscopic momentum correlations probe low-energy interactions of short-lived charmed hadrons that are inaccessible to conventional scattering experiments. We calculate the correlation functions of $D^{+}D^{+}$, $D^{0}D^{0}$, $D^{+}D^{0}$, and $\Lambda_c^+\Lambda_c^+$ in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.02$~TeV, using species-dependent non-Gaussian PHSD sources constructed from hadronization points and strong interactions calibrated to lattice-QCD scattering lengths: OBE and EFT-contact models for $DD$, and an EFT-contact model for $\Lambda_c\Lambda_c$. Coulomb and quantum-statistical effects are included consistently. Although the calibrated interactions are weakly repulsive, the channels separate the relevant effects: $D^{+}D^{0}$, free of Coulomb distortion and identical-particle interference, gives the cleanest access to the $DD$ strong interaction, whereas $\Lambda_c^+\Lambda_c^+$ is most pronounced in peripheral collisions, where the compact source enhances the low-momentum signal. The $\Lambda_c\Lambda_c$ input is taken from lattice QCD at a nonphysical pion mass, so its physical-point shift is not quantified here. Within these stated inputs, the results provide ALICE-ready benchmark correlations and background references; the quoted bands propagate only the lattice scattering-length uncertainty.
papers.reason: Calculates femtoscopic momentum correlation functions for lightest charmed hadrons using lattice-QCD scattering lengths, highly relevant for low-energy hadronic interactions.

papers.title: Direct Urca process facilitated by non-Fermi-liquid quantum criticality
papers.abstract: Conventional Fermi-liquid theories of dense nuclear matter predict that the direct Urca process requires a proton fraction above a threshold of $Y_p \approx 0.11$--$0.15$, which is rarely reached in low-mass neutron stars. Here we show that this stringent kinematic constraint is drastically relaxed by the non-Fermi liquid behavior arising from superfluid and superconducting quantum criticality in neutron stars. In the non-Fermi-liquid regimes, nucleons have a smooth momentum occupation without a sharp Fermi surface, and their chemical potentials develop a logarithmic temperature dependence. These intrinsic features fundamentally alter the standard $\beta$-equilibrium relation. Consequently, direct Urca neutrino emission can be activated even at low nuclear densities. This modifies the long-standing Urca-threshold paradigm and indicates that direct Urca process has the opportunity to occur in low-mass neutron stars.
papers.reason: Shows that non-Fermi liquid behavior from quantum criticality in neutron stars relaxes kinematic constraints on the direct Urca neutrino emission process.

papers.title: Possible Microscopic source of torsion
papers.abstract: Axial fermionic interactions connect vacuum condensation with torsionful back- grounds. We consider a quartic spin spin interaction whose mean field reduction yields a quadratic fermionic Hamiltonian. Its diagonalisation defines a particle and antiparticle condensate, while self consistency determines whether the vacuum devel- ops a non zero axial current. Cutoff, fluctuation and energy conditions delimit the validity of the approximation. When torsion couples to spin, this axial expectation value can provide a microscopic source for an axial torsion background. We then consider mixed Dirac fields on such a background. In the explicit neutrino analysis, metric curvature is neglected while torsion modifies the flavour Bogoliubov coeffi- cients, producing spin dependent oscillation frequencies, condensate densities and CP asymmetries.
papers.reason: Examines axial fermionic interactions generating torsion backgrounds and explicitly analyzes neutrino flavor oscillations, Bogoliubov coefficients, and CP asymmetries in torsionful backgrounds.

papers.title: Probing the $\tau$ anomalous magnetic and electric dipole moments in photon-induced $\gamma\gamma\to\tau^+\tau^-$ production at the FCC-hh
papers.abstract: The sensitivity of the FCC-hh to the anomalous magnetic moment $a_\tau$ and the electric dipole moment $d_\tau$ of the $\tau$ lepton is studied in photon-induced $\gamma\gamma\to\tau^+\tau^-$ production with both $\tau$ leptons decaying hadronically. Central exclusive (elastic) signal events, in which both protons remain intact, are generated with MadGraph5_aMC@NLO using a FeynRules UFO model of the anomalous $\gamma\tau\tau$ vertex merged with the TauDecay model, so that the $\tau$ decays and their spin correlations are included in the matrix element. Single- and double-dissociative production is estimated with SuperChic and added to the elastic signal with its own coupling dependence and with normalisation and shape uncertainties of 25%. Pythia 8 decays the unstable hadrons in the signal, decays the $\tau$ leptons and simulates the parton shower and hadronisation in the backgrounds, and hadronises the dissociated protons. Signal and backgrounds are passed through the Delphes simulation of the FCC-hh detector. Hadronic $\tau$ decays are reconstructed from particle-flow tracks and photons with an algorithm based on the hadrons-plus-strips approach, with an efficiency of 73.4% within the acceptance. Requiring no additional tracks from the $\tau$ vertices retains part of the dissociative contribution and reduces the Drell-Yan and $\gamma\gamma\to WW$ backgrounds to 0.9% of the SM yield. The couplings are constrained from the shape of the total transverse mass distribution. For a centre-of-mass energy of 84 TeV and 30 ab$^{-1}$, the expected 95% CL limits are $-3.38\times10^{-4} < a_\tau < 3.36\times10^{-4}$ and $|d_\tau| < 1.88\times10^{-18}\,e\,$cm, about an order of magnitude beyond the current bounds. Results are also given for FCC-hh scenarios between 72 and 120 TeV and for an optimistic detector parametrisation.
papers.reason: Studies the sensitivity of the FCC-hh to $\tau$ anomalous magnetic and electric dipole moments using photon-induced $\gamma\gamma \to \tau^+\tau^-$ with full spin correlations.

papers.title: Automation of amplitude-level QED resummation with ACRAIC
papers.abstract: Precision electroweak predictions for future $e^+e^-$ colliders will require levels of precision unmatched in collider physics and the modelling of multiple-photon emissions, and the exponentiation of the associated logarithms needs to be carefully considered. The Yennie-Frautschi-Suura theorem subtracts the infrared singularities to all orders and exponentiates them, leaving infrared-finite remainders which can be calculated order-by-order. Coherent exponentiation performs this subtraction at the amplitude level, preserving the interference between emissions, but has so far been available only for fermion-pair production, with hand-coded amplitudes. We present ACRAIC, an automated, amplitude-level realization of this subtraction for general scattering processes in Sherpa. This method allows us to construct an $\mathcal{O}(\alpha)$ and $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ amplitude level subtraction scheme, in which the infrared-finite remainders are tree-level helicity amplitudes with partition-dependent propagator shifts, computed by the Berends--Giele recursion, and the one-loop electroweak virtual enters through a per-helicity factor from the loop provider. At $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ two independent matchings agree on the size of the missing higher orders to $\sim10^{-3}$, and the estimated perturbative uncertainty shrinks by about an order of magnitude relative to $\mathcal{O}(\alpha)$.
papers.reason: Presents an automated amplitude-level QED resummation scheme for precision electroweak predictions at future colliders, relevant for precision leptonic scattering modeling.

papers.title: Holographic Calculation of Semileptonic Form Factors and the Isgur--Wise Function for $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}$ Decays
papers.abstract: We present a holographic analysis of the semileptonic decays $B \to D \ell \bar{\nu}_\ell$ and $B_s \to D_s \ell \bar{\nu}_\ell$ within the Softwall Model (SWM) and the Non-Quadratic Softwall Model (NQSWM). We extract the Isgur-Wise function from the overlap integral of bulk wavefunctions, with model parameters fixed by the heavy-light meson spectra. We impose Heavy Quark Symmetry (HQS) at zero recoil and address the apparent paradox of a non-conserved electroweak current dual to a massless bulk vector field. We argue that the non-conservation, arising from explicit flavor-- symmetry breaking by quark masses, does not generate an anomalous dimension. Hence the bulk field remains massless, and the non-conservation is \emph{encoded} in the independent boundary couplings $g_+$ and $g_-$. Our predictions for the branching fractions are in good agreement with LHCb data for $B_s \to D_s$ decays. The lepton-flavor universality ratios $R(D)$ and $R(D_s)$ are consistent with Standard Model and lattice QCD predictions. We find that the holographic models reproduce the universality of the Isgur-Wise function near zero recoil, while discrepancies at maximum recoil suggest that a more complete treatment of higher-order $1/m_Q$ corrections is needed.
papers.reason: Applies holographic softwall models to extract Isgur-Wise functions and semileptonic form factors for $B \to D$ decays, offering a theoretical perspective on heavy-quark transitions.

papers.title: Four-loop electron EDM matching and timelike $\tau$ electric dipole form factor
papers.abstract: We compute the four-loop matching of a CP-odd four-$\tau$ interaction onto the electron electric dipole moment (EDM), together with the leading timelike $\tau$ dipole form factor generated by the same source. Both results are scale independent at this order. Without a local electron dipole, exact electron-EDM cancellation still leaves a timelike $\tau$ signal proportional to the four-$\tau$ coefficient. Its absorptive part cannot be canceled by a real local dipole, allowing collider limits to constrain the cancellation direction and complement static electron-EDM searches.
papers.reason: Computes four-loop electron EDM matching and timelike $\tau$ electric dipole form factors from a CP-odd four-$\tau$ interaction, connecting precision searches with collider signals.

papers.title: $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda \ell^+\ell^-$ and $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda^{\ast} \ell^+\ell^-$ decays with polarized leptons
papers.abstract: We present an analysis of lepton polarization observables in the rare flavor-changing neutral current decays $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda\ell^+\ell^-$ and $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda^*\ell^+\ell^-$. These decays are driven by the quark-level transition $b \to s\ell^+\ell^-$ and are sensitive to short-distance physics within and beyond the Standard Model. We work within an effective Hamiltonian framework and derive single lepton polarization asymmetries, double lepton polarization asymmetries, and polarized forward-backward asymmetries using the helicity method. The observables are expressed in terms of transversity amplitudes and evaluated using state-of-the-art lattice QCD form factors. We analyze the $q^2$ dependence of several observables for both the ground-state $\Lambda$ and the excited $\Lambda^*(1520)$ final states and discuss sensitivities of the observables to chiral structure of the effective operators and complex Wilson coefficients.
papers.reason: Analyzes lepton polarization observables in $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda \ell^+\ell^-$ using lattice QCD form factors, intersecting with heavy-baryon form factor techniques.

papers.title: Probing Lepton Flavor Violation at FCC-ee
papers.abstract: We investigate the prospects for probing Lepton Flavor Violation (LFV) at FCC-ee within the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) framework. The approximately $2 \times 10^{11}$ $\tau$-lepton pairs expected at the $Z$-pole run of FCC-ee could improve current limits on the branching fractions of $\tau\to3\ell$ and $\tau\to\ell\gamma$ ($\ell=e,\mu$) by factors ranging from 30 to 800, depending on the specific channel. We compare the resulting new-physics reach with that obtained from searches for $Z \to \tau \ell$ and $h \to \tau \ell$, which have so far received greater attention in studies of LFV at future $e^+e^-$ colliders. We find that $\tau$ decays can surpass both the current and the projected sensitivity of $Z\to\tau\ell$ searches to the same LFV interactions, while probing a broader range of SMEFT operators. We further show that, for LFV Yukawa-like interactions, direct searches for $h\to\tau\ell$ provide the strongest sensitivity. By contrast, for semileptonic operators that radiatively induce LFV Higgs decays, this hierarchy can be reversed, with $\tau$ decays providing the leading probe.
papers.reason: Evaluates prospects for probing Lepton Flavor Violation in tau decays and Z/Higgs poles at FCC-ee within SMEFT.

papers.title: Illuminating Light Dark Matter with Fixed-Target Experiments
papers.abstract: Astronomical and cosmological observations provide overwhelming evidence for a non-luminous matter component, dark matter (DM), whose particle nature remains unknown. Experimental searches for non-gravitational DM interactions have largely targeted DM with GeV-TeV masses via nuclear recoils, yielding no discovery thus far. DM in the MeV-GeV mass range, however, is theoretically motivated, reproducing the observed relic abundance while remaining invisible to nuclear recoil searches. Such light DM is better probed via electron recoils or at fixed-target experiments. This thesis advances the theoretical and statistical toolkit for light DM searches at fixed-target experiments, spanning model building, statistical inference, global fits, and signal simulation. We survey the landscape of fixed-target searches for light DM, focusing on the Light Dark Matter eXperiment (LDMX). We also simulate DM signatures at the next-generation experiment SHiP to assess its sensitivity. Within minimal DM models, we present a likelihood-based statistical framework for LDMX using the full two-dimensional recoil electron distribution, spanning exclusion, discovery, parameter estimation, and model comparison in frequentist and Bayesian formulations. This establishes the discovery potential of LDMX, and we quantify the direct detection exposure needed to independently confirm a potential signal. Beyond this paradigm, we perform global fits of scalar and fermionic light DM, combining cosmological, astrophysical, and laboratory constraints. We then extend fixed-target searches to spin-1 DM and higher electromagnetic moment dark photons, yielding rich signatures with strong complementarity to other probes. Finally, we go beyond standard nuclear modelling of dark photon production, incorporating elastic nuclear form factors and spectral functions from many-body ab initio methods in place of analytic treatments.
papers.reason: Advances theoretical and statistical toolkits for light dark matter searches at fixed-target experiments like LDMX and SHiP.

papers.title: Non-Classicality in $tW$ system via negativity and geometric quantum discord
papers.abstract: We perform a phenomenological study of non-classical correlations in the mixed-dimensional qubit-qutrit system realized by leading order $pp\to tW$ production at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV in the leptonic final state. The two missing neutrinos are reconstructed with conditional normalizing flows trained on simulated detector-level objects, and the joint spin density matrix $\rho_{tW}\in\mathcal{H}_2\otimes\mathcal{H}_3$ is obtained in a generalized Bloch representation from the angular distributions of the leptonic decay products. Non-classical correlations are quantified using the Peres--Horodecki negativity and geometric quantum discord. We quantify the correlations at different region of $m_{tW}$ at the reconstruction level within the Standard Model and the impact of two reducible backgrounds viz. $t\bar{t}$ and $WWj$ processes, tagged using boosted decision trees. We further study the behavior of correlations in presence of anomalous chromomagnetic and chromoelectric dipole moments of the top quark. The sensitivity reach of the quantum observables along with polarization and spin correlation parameters are reported for current LHC and future HL-LHC scenario.
papers.reason: Quantifies non-classical correlations (negativity and geometric quantum discord) in leptonic pp -> tW processes with neutrino reconstruction.

papers.title: Charmed baryon decays at BESIII
papers.abstract:
BESIII has accumulated 6.4~fb$^{-1}$ of $e^+e^-$ collision data at center-of-mass energies from 4.60 to 4.95~GeV, corresponding to the world's largest sample of $\Lambda_c^+ ar\Lambda_c^-$ pairs. This proceeding summarizes recent BESIII results on charmed baryon decays, including the first observation of the transverse polarization of the $\Lambda_c^+$ in $e^+e^-	o\Lambda_c^+ ar\Lambda_c^-$, a precision measurement of the inclusive decay $\Lambda_c^+	o\Lambda X$, the first observations of $\Lambda_c^+	o ne^+
u_e$ and $\Lambda_c^+	o n\pi^+\eta$ with deep-learning techniques, the first observation of $\Lambda_c^+	o pK^-e^+
u_e$ together with evidence for $\Lambda_c^+	o\Sigma^\pm\pi^\mp e^+
u_e$, and partial wave analyses of $\Lambda_c^+	o\Lambda\pi^+\eta$.
papers.reason: Summarizes recent BESIII results on charmed baryon decays, including semileptonic Lambda_c decays and polarization measurements directly relevant to low-energy weak interactions.

papers.title: Peripheral nucleon-nucleon scattering with explicit vector mesons in chiral perturbation theory
papers.abstract: Background: In chiral perturbation theory (ChPT), heavy degrees of freedom are integrated out, with their contributions absorbed into low-energy constants. Keeping the $\rho$ and $\omega$ explicit within ChPT retains the finite-range momentum dependence associated with these mesons. Purpose: We study how explicit $\rho$ and $\omega$ mesons affect peripheral $NN$ phase shifts. Methods: We incorporate the vector mesons by counting their masses as hard and the momentum they carry as soft. The next-to-next-to-leading-order nuclear force includes, in addition to one- and two-pion exchange, one-vector-meson exchange with dressed propagators and vertex functions. The vector propagators and vertex functions are fixed from the mesonic sector and the nucleon electromagnetic form factors. We calculate neutron--proton scattering with $J=3$--$5$ up to $T_{\rm lab}=300$ MeV and examine the sensitivity to one-pion-exchange iteration and the spectral-function regularization scheme. Results: The vector-meson contribution falls rapidly with $J$. In several $J=3$ waves it moves the phase shifts toward PWA93, while in other waves the change is small or moves the phase shift away. In ${}^{3}\mathrm{G}_{3}$ the change toward PWA93 persists under variations of the spectral cutoff, and its size is nearly independent of the treatment of one-pion exchange. The ${}^{3}\mathrm{D}_{3}$ wave is strongly cutoff dependent, and there the $\omega$ contribution outweighs the opposing $\rho$ contribution. The tensor and spin-spin components of the $\rho$ interaction play the dominant roles in moving $\epsilon_3$ and ${}^{1}\mathrm{F}_{3}$ toward PWA93, respectively. Conclusions: The effect of the explicit vector mesons on the peripheral phase shifts is channel dependent. The $\rho$ meson gives the dominant shifts toward PWA93, particularly in $\epsilon_3$ and ${}^{3}\mathrm{G}_{3}$.
papers.topic: Explicit Vector Mesons in NN Scattering
papers.reason: Studies peripheral nucleon-nucleon scattering with explicit rho and omega vector mesons in chiral perturbation theory, connecting to nuclear forces.

papers.title: Information Geometry of DGLAP Evolution: From Geodesic Tests to Emergent Small-Circle Geometry
papers.abstract: We investigate the geometric structure of leading-order (LO) nonsinglet DGLAP evolution on the Fisher--Rao manifold of normalized valence distributions, asking whether the QCD-selected trajectory is geodesic and how its departure from geodesic motion is organized. Through the isometric embedding $\Phi=2\sqrt{p}$, the evolution is represented as a curve on a Hilbert sphere of radius two, with its velocity and acceleration determined directly by the DGLAP operator. For a GRV98-based total-valence trajectory over $2\leq Q^2\leq 2000~{\rm GeV}^2$, we find a nonzero but weakly scale-dependent geodesic curvature. An arc-length-weighted principal-component analysis shows that two affine directions capture more than $99.999\%$ of the trajectory variance. The corresponding affine plane intersects the Fisher sphere in a small circle, whose predicted geodesic curvature closely agrees with that reconstructed from the DGLAP-generated acceleration. An $x$-resolved analysis further reveals that Fisher motion is governed by relative PDF reshaping rather than probability weight alone, with different momentum-fraction regions contributing to motion along the trajectory and its transverse bending. The Mellin representation provides a complementary perspective on the effective dimensional reduction through the collective evolution of the spectral hierarchy. These results establish a quantitative information-geometric characterization of the reference LO DGLAP trajectory and reveal an organized, near-small-circle structure over the finite evolution interval.
papers.reason: Applies information geometry and Fisher-Rao manifolds to analyze the geometric structure and trajectories of LO DGLAP evolution of parton distributions.

papers.title: Displaced e+e- Signatures from an X17-Mediated Inelastic Dark-Sector Cascade
papers.abstract: We investigate displaced electron-positron signatures from an inelastic dark sector mediated by a light vector boson associated with the X17 anomaly. A heavy neutral fermion decays into a lighter stable state and the mediator, whose subsequent decay produces a single visible vertex after two stages of neutral propagation. We calculate the decay width, displacement distribution, lepton kinematics, and production rate in electro-positron collisions, including vector polarization. At Belle II, stronger dark-sector couplings increase production but require finely adjusted masses to preserve a macroscopic decay length. We quantify off-shell contributions and assess the validity of the two-body approximation. We show that the electron-positron pair cannot satisfy simultaneously the moment and opening-angle cuts of an existing search proposal for the configuration studied. Less restrictive selections allow nonzero kinematic acceptance. Our results clarify the experimental requirements for searching these signatures at Belle II.
papers.reason: Investigates displaced electron-positron signatures and kinematics from an inelastic dark sector mediated by an X17 anomaly vector boson.

papers.title: Deciphering Entangled Fission at Finite Excitations via Thermal Subspace Projection
papers.abstract: The sharing of particles and energy between entangled fission fragments is known to contribute considerably to final observable distributions. This work unravels this sharing mechanism at finite excitations, which exhibits an intriguing quantum-thermal interplay relevant to long-standing open questions in induced fission. We formulate a thermal double particle-number projection onto spatial subspaces, using the Balian-Brezin representation and Grassmann integrals, to derive the projected partition function and observables. Based on finite-temperature dynamical fission calculations of 240Pu, the formalism explains the puzzling energy dependence of odd-even staggering in charge yields and of sawtooth neutron multiplicities. The present framework also provides a general projection tool for probing entangled thermal many-body systems.
papers.reason: Formulates a thermal particle-number projection to explain energy-dependent odd-even staggering and neutron multiplicities in entangled fission fragments.

papers.title: Information geometry of DGLAP evolution
papers.abstract: Quark and gluon splittings shift proton momentum toward smaller fractions with increasing resolution. Momentum conservation makes the summed momentum-weighted quark and gluon densities, when nonnegative, a probability distribution. We apply information geometry, the geometry of probability distributions, to this probabilistic form of Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi evolution. We evaluate, to our knowledge for the first time, the speed at which the shape of the proton's momentum distribution changes, measured by how well distributions at neighboring resolutions can be told apart statistically. At leading order, with one-loop splitting functions and running coupling, five fixed quark flavors, nonnegative quark and gluon densities and sufficiently regular inputs, we obtain a closed-form lower bound on this speed. Once the coupling is specified, three numbers of the input (the distribution at the starting resolution) fix the bound at every scale without computing the evolved distribution. For three of the five model inputs at four scales from 2 GeV to 10 TeV, the squared bound is at least 94.8 percent of the squared speed. The bound is reached when the distribution's relative rate of change is linear in the logarithm of the inverse momentum fraction. For these three model inputs at the four scales, the relative rate of change is close to this linear form in mean square weighted by momentum.
papers.reason: Applies information geometry to evaluate the statistical distinguishability and speed of shape change in DGLAP parton evolution.

papers.title: A Catalog of Lepton Mass Textures from Koide and Alikhanov Relations
papers.abstract: The empirical Koide relation for charged-lepton masses and the recently proposed Alikhanov relation for neutrino mass-squared differences offer intriguing hints toward understanding the structure of lepton mass matrices. Motivated by these observations, we systematically explore charged-lepton and neutrino mass-matrix textures that satisfy these relations and confront their predictions for lepton mixing with experimental data. For the charged-lepton sector, we investigate representative positive Hermitian square-root matrices classified by the number of common eigenvector directions of their generators: three, one, or none. For the neutrino sector, an exhaustive enumeration of real symmetric integer matrices with entries between $-5$ and $5$ identifies six signed-permutation classes with $m_1=0$ and six with $m_1>0$ that satisfy the Alikhanov relation. Combining these neutrino textures with the charged-lepton constructions, allowing for different relative flavor orientations and phase alignments, yields $400$ viable structural pairs consistent with the measured lepton mixing parameters. All retained solutions satisfy the adopted cosmological bound on the sum of neutrino masses and existing laboratory constraints. In particular, the full-rank neutrino textures predict $m_1\simeq16.77$-$17.22\,\mathrm{meV}$. Representative viable solutions yield effective Majorana masses $m_{\beta\beta}\simeq1.29$-$4.03\,\mathrm{meV}$ and $4.07$-$18.67\,\mathrm{meV}$ for the $m_1=0$ and $m_1>0$ branches, respectively, providing potential targets for future high-sensitivity searches.
papers.reason: Systematically explores lepton mass matrix textures satisfying Koide and Alikhanov relations, offering a purely phenomenological study of neutrino and charged-lepton mass generation.

papers.title: Hybrid Stars with Different Amount of Quark Matter
papers.abstract: In a previous work, we explored the possibility of neutron stars with large quark cores. Through Bayesian inference, we obtained large sets of equations of state imposing constraints regarding the properties of nuclear matter, mass-radius data from NICER, the GW170817 data from Virgo-LIGO collaboration, perturbative QCD and causality. We also imposed that the maximum mass neutron star (NS$\text{max}$) must have a large quark core. In this work, we obtain a new set of equations of state (SmallQ set) with the same constraints as before. However, we relaxed the last constraint, imposing only that NS$\text{max}$ must have quark core, regardless of its size. We compare the results with the set from our previous paper constrained by NICER and GW170817 observations NJL-GW. For both sets, we use the Relativistic Mean Field model with nonlinear meson interactions for the hadron phase and the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model with four- and eight-quark interaction terms for the quark phase. The SmallQ set has higher values of phase transition density, with 3 -- 4.5 $\rho_0$, compared to the NJL-GW, with 2 -- 2.5 $\rho_0$. The new set describes NSs with smaller radius and smaller tidal deformability, and is more compatible with NICER and GW170817 data. A difference in the quark matter composition is observed, with a larger quark strange fraction occurring in the SmallQ set. Within this set, $2 M_\odot$ NSs may contain little to no quark matter. It is shown that there is a non negligible fraction of EOS whose mass-radius curve presents a positive slope for 1.8 $M_\odot$ stars, while for nucleonic stars this fraction is negligible and for hyperonic stars the slope is always negative.
papers.reason: Explores neutron star equations of state with quark cores using Bayesian inference and RMF/NJL models, providing nuclear matter constraints relevant for dense matter physics.

papers.title: Magnetic-field dependence of the QCD electric screening mass parameter through $g^4$ in hot and dense matter
papers.abstract: A constant magnetic field modifies the hard electric screening sector of hot and dense QCD and generates a directional splitting at $\mathcal{O}(g^4)$. We determine the strict-hard screening pole through $g^4$ for three massless flavors with physical $u,d,s$ charges, retaining the full $eB/T^2$ dependence without a weak- or strong-field expansion. The shifted-frequency construction used for the two-loop exchange contribution is a background-field Feynman-gauge curvature; we derive and apply its local conversion to the ordinary Feynman-gauge self-energy before assembling the screening pole. The leading magnetic shift is isotropic, while the $g^4$ directional splitting arises from the one-loop anisotropic kinetic normalization; the symmetry-allowed finite-density $A_0F_{12}$ mixing is numerically small over the studied range for physical $u,d,s$ charges. For $\mu/T=0$ and $1$, the magnetic $g^4$ coefficient is positive over $0\le eB/T^2\le4$ and is strongly reduced by density. Extending the calculation to $0\le\mu/T\le2$ at $eB/T^2=1$ and $4$ reveals sign reversals of both the leading magnetic coefficient and the directional splitting at sufficiently large density. The zero-field limit reproduces the Braaten-Nieto result and its finite-density extension by Vuorinen. The running coupling used only for the phenomenological magnetic mass shift is chosen independently of $B$, so that all magnetic-field dependence through $g^4$ resides in the calculated coefficients.
papers.reason: Determines the magnetic-field dependence of the QCD electric screening mass through $g^4$ in hot and dense matter using background-field techniques.

papers.title: Shell-model description of collective deformation variables $\beta$ and $\gamma$ in $^{164-188}$Hf nuclei
papers.abstract: Symmetry-based models, such as the pseudo-SU(3) scheme, have proved to be highly useful tools for describing the low-energy structure of nuclei in the rare-earth region. This model is employed to study the evolution of the collective deformation variables beta and gamma in the ground state (0+) along the isotopic chain 164-188Hf. The truncation is carried out by considering the irreducible representations (irreps) with high spatial symmetry and pseudo-spin 0 and 1, so that both the most and less symmetric relevant irreps are included, the latter being of particular importance for the description of low-energy properties, especially the shape transition. The Hamiltonian includes spherical Nilsson single-particle energies, the quadrupole-quadrupole interaction, and pairing correlations. It is parameterised in a systematic manner, so that the description is obtained without free parameters. In agreement with experimental data, the maximum deformation beta occurs at N = 100, although the model predicts values that are about 20% smaller. As in other theoretical studies, a prolate deformation (gamma = 8o) is predicted for almost all nuclei in the shell, with a clear transition towards triaxial shapes for N > 110. An analysis of the effects of the pairing and Nilsson terms on the values of $\beta$ and gamma indicates that it is the latter that determine the prolate-oblate transition, with the pairing term playing only a marginal role. The absence of nucleons in the intruder sector is the most significant limitation of the model.
papers.reason: Applies a pseudo-SU(3) shell-model framework to study collective deformation variables in Hf isotopic chains without free parameters.

papers.title: Annihilation feedback on elastic scattering in self-interacting dark matter
papers.abstract: Sizable dark-matter self-interactions, motivated by observations of galactic structure, often arise from the exchange of light force mediators. Light mediators can render scattering nonperturbative and make inelastic processes important. Unitarity, via the optical theorem, implies that elastic and inelastic interactions cannot be treated independently: inelasticity induces absorptive contributions to the two-particle self-energy kernel that determines the elastic amplitude, while the resulting incoming-state dynamics also modifies the inelastic amplitudes. We study the feedback of dark-matter annihilation on elastic scattering in the presence of a long-range force. Although annihilation is a short-distance process, it can be strongly enhanced by such a force. We find that its feedback becomes significant near Sommerfeld resonances, where it suppresses the low-velocity growth of the baseline elastic cross section. Near baseline elastic-scattering zeros, it may instead generate a nonzero elastic floor required by unitarity. A companion paper studies the feedback of radiative bound-state formation on elastic scattering, which can generate sizable self-interactions.
papers.reason: Studies how dark matter annihilation feedback affects elastic scattering and Sommerfeld enhancements, relevant to dark matter phenomenology.

papers.title: A Natural Dark Matter-Dark Energy Interaction from Axion-Monopole Dynamics
papers.abstract: We propose a natural framework for interacting dark matter and dark energy based on axion-monopole dynamics in a dark gauge sector. Dark matter is composed of dark 't Hooft-Polyakov monopoles, while dark energy is an ultralight axion whose coupling to the dark gauge field induces an axion-dependent dyon mass through the Witten effect. This generates a direct dark matter-dark energy interaction. We show that generic models with a significant dark matter-dark energy coupling suffer from a naturalness problem: the Coleman-Weinberg potential induced by the interaction is typically much larger than the dark energy scale. In our model, the corrections arise from a monodromy tower of dyon states, allowing them to be exponentially suppressed. In the minimal setup, the interaction strength is predicted to be $\sim 0.1\%$, below the sensitivity of current observations. We discuss scenarios in which cosmological population of higher-charge dyons can enhance the interaction to the percent level, producing an apparent phantom dark energy equation of state. We further show that the parameter space of the axion-monopole model preferred by fitting the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) results can also naturally explain the cosmic birefringence with a small anomaly coefficient.
papers.reason: Proposes a dark matter-dark energy interaction framework from axion-monopole dynamics and the Witten effect.

papers.title: Cosmic birefringence from a stiff axion field and its cosmological implications
papers.abstract: We propose a model in which the observed cosmic microwave background birefringence arises from the interaction of photons with a stiff ($w=1$) pseudo-scalar field that today contributes a subdominant fraction of the total energy density, distinct from both dark matter and dark energy. Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constrains the cosmological density of the stiff field, leading to a lower bound for its coupling with photons, $g_{\phi\gamma} > 8.9 \times 10^{-14}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. Photon conversion in cluster-hosted quasars sets an upper bound, $g_{\phi\gamma} < 5.0 \times 10^{-13}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. Therefore, there is a narrow window for the discovery of this cosmological component that can be explored in the forthcoming years with astrophysical axion searches. Moreover, we show that this scenario leads to gravitational-wave signals that can be tested with planned experiments.
papers.reason: Proposes a model where CMB birefringence arises from photon interaction with a stiff pseudo-scalar field.

papers.title: Self-interacting dark matter from radiative bound-state-formation feedback
papers.abstract: Observations of galactic structure motivate sizable dark-matter self-interactions at low velocities, naturally realized through light force mediators. Such mediators can also make inelastic processes very efficient. Unitarity then requires their absorptive contributions to the two-particle self-energy kernel to be resummed, which in turn feeds back into both the elastic and inelastic scattering amplitudes. We study the feedback of radiative bound-state formation on elastic scattering and its implications for self-interacting dark matter. We focus on capture processes through emission of a charged scalar; such transitions are particularly efficient because the scattering and bound states are governed by different effective potentials, a feature also shared by radiative capture through emission of a non-Abelian gauge boson. We show that their feedback can generate sizable elastic scattering relevant for halo dynamics, even when the baseline elastic amplitude vanishes. Notably, the generated elastic cross section can grow toward low velocities, resembling long-range scattering. A companion paper examines the feedback from annihilation processes.
papers.reason: Analyzes the feedback of radiative bound-state formation on elastic scattering cross sections for self-interacting dark matter.

papers.title: The Electron-Recoil Response Tail and the LZ High-Energy Event Background
papers.abstract: We reconstruct the continuum electron-recoil contribution to the LZ background expectation from the collaboration's released simulation configuration. The released model specifies a definite response tail, but the published calibration information supplies no bound on how far the physical tail may depart from it at the probabilities the expectation depends on. Distributions reproducing the executable model's mean, variance, and standardised skewness exactly, and its event-conditioned 10, 50, and 90\% \(N_e\) quantiles to about one per cent, differ in the relevant tail probability by more than five orders of magnitude. The ladder is short: a tail agreeing with that central characterisation to 0.14\% in the quantiles lifts the electron-recoil contribution out of the negligible range, and one agreeing to 0.47\% makes it comparable to the entire background quoted for the comparison region. We go on to identify the measurements that would settle it.
papers.reason: Reconstructs continuum electron-recoil background response tails for the LZ experiment, relevant to low-energy dark matter/neutrino detectors.

papers.title: Jets as differential probes of hot QCD matter
papers.abstract: Ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions create short-lived droplets of deconfined, hot QCD matter whose evolution connects far-from-equilibrium early dynamics to the hydrodynamic quark-gluon plasma. High-energy jets, produced in early hard scatterings and modified by this evolving medium, provide multi-scale probes of its microscopic properties. This thesis develops perturbative QCD tools to extract information about hot QCD matter from its imprint on differential jet substructure observables. Our framework is the BDMPS-Z description of high-energy partons propagating through stochastic colour fields. We first study anisotropic QCD matter by replacing the usual scalar broadening parameter with direction-dependent transverse momentum broadening. This relates anisotropic corrections to medium-induced splittings to spin information and azimuthal patterns in final-state energy flow. Energy correlators are then used as observables sensitive to these effects, including heavy-flavour EECs, azimuthally differential EECs and clover projections designed to isolate leading anisotropy-induced harmonics. We also examine how energy loss affects the interpretation of jet substructure modifications. Quantile matching defines reconstructed energy loss as a population-level shift between vacuum and medium-modified jet spectra. We further develop energy-loss functions, which encode the distribution of energy retained by jet-originated hadrons, and show how their moments enter multi-point projected energy correlators. Finally, we go beyond single $1\to2$ medium-induced splittings by studying spin-induced correlations between successive emissions and higher-point energy correlators including contributions from medium response. The results show that differential jet substructure can probe directional properties of QCD matter and multi-point dynamics of jets propagating through it.
papers.reason: Develops perturbative QCD tools using differential jet substructure and BDMPS-Z energy correlators to probe hot QCD matter.

papers.title: Pretraining on boosted boson decays for polarization tagging of hadronic $W$ bosons
papers.abstract: Longitudinally polarized weak bosons probe the unitarization of vector-boson scattering. At large boosts, longitudinal and transverse $W$ bosons produce jets with the same mass and two-prong structure, distinguished only by the decay angle. Longitudinal bosons are rare: they occur in only 0.3% of $W$+jet events at these large boosts. We ask where the polarization information of a boosted $W$ boson lies and how much a tagger can recover. Requiring both decay quarks within the jet truncates the decay-angle distribution at an edge set by $m/(p_T R)$, which we show bounds any hadronic polarization tagger. Within this acceptance, the decay angle carries essentially all the polarization information of a jet in $W$+jet events. Polarized samples are costly to simulate for vector-boson scattering, so we pretrain a point-edge transformer on $10^7$ unpolarized jets of boosted bosons, top quarks and QCD and test how much it recovers from few labels. Fine-tuned on 783 labeled jets per class with its transformer blocks kept fixed, the network pretrained to classify these jets improves on training from scratch, but generic pretraining on a broad mix of jets and a boosted decision tree on substructure observables do as well. The best taggers recover most, but not all, of the separation the decay angle allows, and student networks with a few hundred times fewer parameters, trained by knowledge distillation, match their teacher. More information lies outside the jet. The production angle, reconstructed with the recoiling jet, improves every tagger. In diboson production and vector-boson scattering at matrix-element level, the production kinematics carry more information than the decay angles of both bosons. Trading the generality of a jet tagger for an event-level tagger trained on the process thus brings significant gains, which measurements of longitudinal vector-boson scattering could exploit.
papers.reason: Investigates polarization tagging of boosted hadronic W bosons via decay angles and point-edge transformers for vector-boson scattering studies.

papers.title: Dynamical Triaxial Correlations in the Charge Radii of Neutron-Rich Ruthenium Isotopes
papers.abstract: Nuclear charge radii are fundamental observables that track changes in nuclear structure. Recent measurements of neutron-rich Ru isotopes, interpreted using mean-field density-functional calculations, have highlighted the sensitivity of charge radii to static triaxial deformation. Whether dynamical shape fluctuations involving triaxial configurations---known to affect both nuclear ground- and excited-state properties---can reshape the charge-radii evolution remains unresolved. In this Letter, we investigate the charge radii of even-even neutron-rich $^{106-114}$Ru within a nuclear density-functional framework that combines three-dimensional angular-momentum projection with the generator-coordinate method. Including dynamical triaxial shape fluctuations yields charge radii in good agreement with experiment, without introducing additional adjustable parameters. By successively incorporating static triaxial deformation, dynamical axial shape fluctuations, and dynamical triaxial shape fluctuations, we trace how the predicted charge radii change at each step. These results demonstrate that triaxial shape dynamics can leave a substantial imprint on charge radii. They also inform the interpretation of experimental charge-radius measurements used to trace the evolution of nuclear structure, since charge radii alone cannot uniquely determine the underlying nuclear shape.
papers.reason: Investigates nuclear charge radii and dynamical triaxial shape fluctuations in neutron-rich Ruthenium isotopes using density-functional theory.

papers.title: Flavor decomposition of electromagnetic multipole moments in $[q_1q_2][\bar q_3 \bar c]$ tetraquarks: Light-quark analogs of $T_{cs1}(2900)^0$ with $J^P = 1^+$
papers.abstract: We present a systematic study of the magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole moments of compact $[q_1 q_2][\bar q_3 \bar c]$ tetraquark states with quantum numbers $J^P = 1^+$, in the diquark--antidiquark picture and within the light-cone QCD sum rule framework. By performing a flavor decomposition across all admissible $u/d$ configurations, we show that the charm-quark contribution to the electromagnetic moments vanishes algebraically at the operator level -- a structural feature of the specific spin organization adopted here, in which the heavy antiquark resides in a pseudoscalar antidiquark, distinct from the dynamical $1/m_c$ suppression operative in alternative compact constructions and in hadronic molecules. The magnetic moments follow a coherent light-flavor pattern -- positive for $uu$-, negative for $dd$-, and suppressed for mixed-flavor diquarks -- and the quadrupole moments are non-zero throughout, corresponding, in the customary geometrical interpretation, to intrinsically deformed charge distributions. We further identify the dimensionless multipole ratio $\mathcal{D}/\mu$ as a structural observable, independent of the normalization of the interpolating current, which probes the relative geometry of the spin-current and charge distributions complementary to the absolute moments. Taken together, the algebraic decoupling of the charm contribution and the operator-level distinction it implies among different singly-heavy tetraquark architectures constitute methodological signatures that discriminate among the corresponding internal organizations and, to the extent that a physical candidate is dominated by one of them, among compact and molecular interpretations.
papers.reason: Presents a QCD sum rule study of magnetic and electric quadrupole moments of singly-heavy tetraquarks with flavor decompositions.

papers.title: Partial reconstruction of the decay $B_{s}^{0}\rightarrow \phi(K^{+}K^{-})\eta' (\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\eta)$
papers.abstract: The decay $B_s^0 \to \phi(K^+K^-)\eta'(\pi^+\pi^-\eta)$ is of particular interest in flavour physics because in the Standard Model it proceeds predominantly through the quark transition $\bar{b} \to \bar{s}s\bar{s}$. However, the reconstruction of this decay is experimentally challenging due to the presence of the neutral $\eta$ particle, which significantly reduces the overall reconstruction efficiency. In this study, the feasibility of using the partial reconstruction technique to reconstruct the invariant mass of the $B_s^0$ meson without explicitly detecting the $\eta$ particle is investigated. Monte Carlo simulated events corresponding to an FCC-ee environment are used, and the effects of detector momentum and vertex resolutions on the reconstruction performance are examined. The results show that improved vertex resolution substantially improves the global reconstructed mass response and partial-reconstruction efficiency, while improvements in momentum resolution are manifested primarily through a narrowing of the fitted central DCB component. These findings suggest that future high-luminosity $e^+e^-$ colliders such as FCC-ee could effectively exploit the partial reconstruction technique to study rare decay modes containing undetected neutral particles.
papers.reason: Investigates the partial reconstruction technique for B_s^0 -> phi eta' decays with undetected neutral particles at FCC-ee.

papers.title: Two-Component Dark Matter and Strongly First-Order Electroweak Phase Transition via a Two-Step Mechanism in the Inert Doublet plus Real Singlet Model
papers.abstract: We study a two-component dark matter model in which a real singlet scalar and an inert doublet scalar are simultaneously present alongside the Standard Model, each stabilized by an independent discrete symmetry. The real singlet undergoes a strong first-order transition at high temperature, establishing an intermediate phase with a non-zero singlet vacuum expectation value, which in turn generates the barrier required for the Higgs field to complete a strongly first-order electroweak transition at a lower temperature. This two-step mechanism naturally enforces the condition $v_c/T_c \geq 1$, the sphaleron washout-avoidance criterion necessary for electroweak baryogenesis. The gravitational wave spectrum from both steps is computed; the second step produces a decihertz signal, peaking near $0.08$--$0.34~\mathrm{Hz}$ across the viable parameter space and $0.14$--$0.22~\mathrm{Hz}$ at the benchmark points, that reaches the sensitivity of DECIGO for the strongest transitions and of BBO more widely, while the first remains sub-threshold for all planned detectors. At the coupling values required to drive the phase transition, the singlet is generically underabundant as a thermal relic, so the inert doublet carries the dominant fraction of the observed relic density. Confronting the model with current constraints, we find that the LUX-ZEPLIN 2024 result excludes the entire electroweak-phase-transition-viable parameter space of the singlet sector across the full mass range, even after rescaling by the singlet relic fraction, establishing a complete no-go for the singlet as a viable thermal dark matter candidate in this framework.
papers.reason: Studies a two-component dark matter model and strong first-order electroweak phase transition via a two-step mechanism.

papers.title: Blueprint for an AI-Enabled Particle Theory Community
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in the capabilities and reach of artificial intelligence (AI) are changing research in particle physics. In this new era, AI is an innovative tool for theoretical physicists, while the interaction of AI and particle theory is itself a developing field. We argue that particle theory requires a community-scale effort to realize its full potential. We show how particle theory occupies a unique position in the AI for physics landscape, and describe the complementarity of AI and theory developments. We conclude with a series of recommendations on how to build an AI-enabled theory community for the Genesis Mission.
authors: George T. Fleming (Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory)
Daniel C. Hackett (Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory)
Can Kilic (University of Texas at Austin)
Tim M. P. Tait (University of California
papers.reason: Outlines a community-scale blueprint for integrating artificial intelligence into particle theory workflows, offering a broad methodological overview.

papers.title: Constraints on Dark Matter Annihilation from Starlight-Induced Inverse Compton Emission in Omega Centauri
papers.abstract: The search for the particle identity of dark matter (DM) remains one of the foremost challenges in modern physics. In this work, we derive new constraints on the DM annihilation cross section $\langle\sigma v\rangle$ by considering the inverse Compton (IC) scattering of DM annihilation injected $e^+e^-$ off the starlight radiation field in Omega Centauri. As a likely remnant core of a dwarf galaxy, Omega Centauri provides a dense stellar environment that enhances the predict IC signal. Using multi-wavelength observations from Chandra and Fermi-LAT, we establish upper limits on $\langle\sigma v\rangle$ over a wide DM mass range from MeV to TeV. Notably, in the tens-of-MeV range, our results surpass existing constraints by approximately two orders of magnitude, exceeding $\langle\sigma v\rangle \sim 10^{-31}~{\rm cm^3\,s^{-1}}$. At several GeV to the TeV DM masses range, our constraints also remain stronger than existing limits. Our results demonstrate that starlight induced IC emission is an important component for indirect DM searches in dense stellar systems, establishing Omega Centauri as a powerful probe of the nature of DM.
papers.reason: Derives constraints on dark matter annihilation cross sections using starlight-induced inverse Compton emission in Omega Centauri across an extensive mass range.

papers.title: Pulse Shape Model for a Light Enhanced Phonon Detector
papers.abstract: COSINUS has tested prototype NaI-based cryogenic scintillating calorimeters with a composite design, in which the transition edge sensor (TES) is fabricated on a separate carrier crystal coupled to the NaI target. Measurements with the composite detectors showed deviations from the known pulse shape description for cryogenic calorimeters and did not reveal an identifiable nuclear recoil population during a neutron calibration. In this work we present a new pulse shape model which provides an explanation to these observations and that laid the foundation for the development of the final COSINUS phonon detector design named remote TES (remoTES). We demonstrate that the first COSINUS detector prototypes featured a phonon channel with signal enhancement by light absorption in the carrier, namely a light enhanced phonon detector. This design offers for the first time the chance to use a single channel phonon detector for particle discrimination. We present recent results using a novel pulse shape fitting method based on the Bayesian inference software package BAT.jl.
papers.reason: Presents a novel pulse-shape model for composite cryogenic NaI scintillating calorimeters (COSINUS) featuring light-enhanced phonon signals for particle discrimination.

papers.title: Floquet Instability of Photon-Axion Conversion
papers.abstract: The discovery of axions would provide evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model. In this work, we investigate axion-photon conversion in the presence of a background magnetic field with simultaneous spatial and temporal periodicity. By performing a Lorentz transformation, the coupled axion-photon system is mapped onto a time-periodic linear system that can be analyzed using Floquet theorem. We find unstable modes associated with resonant crossing between Floquet replicas. The resulting complex Floquet exponents lead to exponentially growing modes, which we identify as a Floquet instability. Then, we determine the parameter regions in which this instability appears in a perturbative analysis. We further show that the Floquet instability enhances the axion-field amplitude generated from an initial photon field. Our results demonstrate that spatiotemporally periodic magnetic backgrounds provide a distinct mechanism for modifying axion-photon conversion through Floquet instability.
papers.reason: Investigates Floquet instabilities in axion-photon conversion using periodic magnetic fields, offering an adjacent BSM mechanism.

papers.title: Deconfinement on $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ and Axion Domain Walls
papers.abstract: We investigate the nontrivial dynamics on $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ domain walls and compute their tension in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) compactified on a circle with $N$ colors and $F < N$ massless fundamental flavors. In the process, we obtain insights on the $\eta'$ meson's potential in a regime where it is heavy and comparable in mass to other QCD resonances, as in Nature. We employ a center-stabilized compactification of QCD on a small circle of size $L$ with color-flavor twisted boundary conditions for the quarks. We demonstrate that probe particles in color representations of $N$-ality $N/\mathrm{gcd}(N,F)$ are deconfined on the $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ domain walls whenever $N$ and $F$ are not coprime. This is reminiscent of deconfinement on axion domain walls in pure Yang--Mills. Finally, in the double scaling limit $N\rightarrow \infty$ keeping $NL$ and $F$ fixed, the infrared spectrum spans an emergent dimension.
